'''William Pitt Durfee''' (5 February 1855 – 17 December 1941) was an American mathematician who introduced [[Durfee square]]s. He was a student of [[James Joseph Sylvester|James Sylvester]], and after obtaining his degree in 1883 he became a professor at [[Hobart and William Smith Colleges|Hobart college]] in 1884 and became dean in 1888. [[Durfee House]] and Durfee Hall are named in his honor.
